subject: Deployment: key ownership, subprocessors & cross-border transfer clarifications
messages:
From: Sofia Burnett <sofia.burnett@heimhealth.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: Heim Health Legal <legal@heimhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment & DPA - key ownership questions

Hi Ava / Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our privacy team reviewed the draft DPA and has three primary asks before we can proceed with procurement:

1) BYOK/Customer-managed keys for on-prem or VPC deployments — we need confirmation that Heim Health holds the key material and that Redwood cannot access plaintext model inputs/outputs without a formal break-glass.
2) Full list of subprocessors and whether any will process data outside the US/EU (we want to know cross-border flows).
3) Operator access policy — specifically how break-glass is audited and whether we can require attestation in the contract.

I attached our earlier subprocessor spreadsheet for reference (subprocessors_list_20280528.csv). Can you share Redwood's subprocessors list and a clear statement on key custody and escrow?

Goal: get legal redlines and a short mutual action plan this week if possible.

Best,
Sofia Burnett
Head of Security & Privacy
Heim Health

Attachment: subprocessors_list_20280528.csv (spreadsheet)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: Sofia Burnett <sofia.burnett@heimhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment & DPA - key ownership questions

Sofia — thanks for the note and the file. Looping in Rachel (legal), Vivek (infra/security), and Jordan (ops) to confirm technical/contract positions.

High-level answers (will formalize in redline):
- BYOK: For Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem packages) we support customer-managed keys via customer KMS (BYOK). Customer retains key material; by default there is no key escrow. Operator break-glass requires documented approval, with an auditable ticket and KMS attestation where feasible.
- Subprocessors: we can provide a current list. Most subprocessors are in the US; a small set (monitoring & observability vendors) may have EU-located processing. We can propose an Annex listing onshore subprocessors and a limited cross-border disclosure.
- Operator access: we have an operator-runbook that only allows ephemeral access for specific troubleshooting; access is logged and requires at least two approvals. We can include stronger contractual commitments (e.g., 30-day notice before any operator action, audit window) if needed.

Vivek — can you confirm if we can provide an HSM attestation (PKCS#11 cert) for the on-prem bundle? Jordan — any concerns about the operational timeline if we add the extra approvals requested by Heim?

Next: Rachel, can you prepare a redline DPA and a short exhibit describing the BYOK flow and subprocessors list? I'll gather the current subprocessor CSV and a diagram.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachment: N/A

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Sofia Burnett <sofia.burnett@heimhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment & DPA - key ownership questions

Sofia / Ava,

I've attached a first-pass redline of the DPA (DPA_HeimHealth_redline_v1.pdf) with notes inline. High-level comments:

- Key custody: We accept BYOK for Redwood Private. Proposed clause: "Customer retains sole control of key material; Redwood shall not (a) request access to plaintext model inputs/outputs, or (b) use keys to decrypt customer data except under an express, auditable break-glass process authorized in writing by Customer." Please confirm exact wording you need for procurement.

- Key escrow: Redwood will not escrow keys absent a separate agreement. If the customer requests escrow for disaster recovery, we require a signed Escrow Addendum with defined access controls.

- Subprocessors: I've added an Annex A placeholder that lists current subprocessors and a process for adding new ones with 30-days notice and an option for the customer to object. For EU customers we can commit to data transfer mechanisms (SCCs) and identify subprocessors that process in the EU vs US.

- Cross-border transfers: default position is customer data is processed in region of deployment. For hosted fallback scenarios we can commit to encrypted-in-transit flows and mandate model-variant policies that avoid export of raw customer PII to other regions without consent.

- Operator access & audit: proposed stronger language around access logging, two-person approval for break-glass, retention of audit logs for 12 months, and SOC2 reports available upon NDA.

I'll attach the redline now. Ava / Vivek: can you add the subprocessor CSV and byok diagram so I can bundle into the exhibit? Sofia: is 12 months log retention sufficient for Heim's audit, or do you need longer?

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_HeimHealth_redline_v1.pdf (PDF redline)

From: Anders Möller <anders.moller@eu-consult.com>
To: Sofia Burnett <sofia.burnett@heimhealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2028 09:45:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Deployment & DPA - key ownership questions

Hi all,

Quick follow on behalf of Heim's procurement/legal review:

- Audit rights: Heim needs contractual audit rights (once per year on reasonable notice) with scope limited to the Private deployment stack. Can Redwood confirm scope and timing? We expect results within 30 days of request.

- HSM/KMS attestation: would be ideal to have a vendor-signed attestation (e.g., HSM firmware version + FIPS/HSM cert) included as an Annex. That addresses our regulators' technical checks.

- For forensic incident response, Heim requires either (a) raw logs exported under a narrow legal process or (b) a platform-provided sanitized view. Please state what options Redwood can offer and whether there are cost/time implications.

Sofia: I'll collate these into a short procurement checklist if you'd like.

Thanks,
Anders Möller
Independent Security Advisor
